title: Anneal requirements translated into semantic obligations
question: Derive acceptance criteria from the principles, including UB freedom, safe-client soundness, correspondence, extensibility, and ordinary-user accessibility.
rationale: A reusable component is useful only if its guarantees satisfy Anneal's promises; these criteria prevent convenience or performance from silently weakening them.

title: The unresolved semantic boundaries of current Anneal
question: Map V1, the redesign, and the PR stack to obligations already established, explicitly trusted, excluded, or still unrepresented.
rationale: This identifies which problems a new foundation must solve and which existing proofs, interfaces, and mathematical models it can retain.

title: Existing evidence and literature coverage
question: Crosswalk the reference corpus and open discussions against this agenda; preserve a bibliography with backward and forward citation searches.
rationale: The corpus already contains substantial evidence. A coverage map avoids duplicate work and exposes missing or newly published research.

title: What different soundness theorems actually establish
question: Compare type safety, non-stuckness, UB freedom, functional correctness, contextual refinement, compiler correctness, and whole-program adequacy.
rationale: These results have different subjects and premises. Their precise meaning determines whether they support the Rust claim Anneal wants to report.

title: A common capability and evaluation matrix
question: Define shared language features, semantic obligations, examples, negative controls, and measurement rules for comparing candidates.
rationale: A common matrix prevents comparisons from favoring tools merely because they verify different programs or weaker properties.

title: Forms of reuse and their costs
question: Compare reusing mathematical ideas, specifications, libraries, source translators, proof engines, certificates, and complete verification pipelines.
rationale: Building on existing work can mean several different integrations, each moving implementation effort, proof obligations, and maintenance elsewhere.

title: End-to-end trust accounting
question: Trace dependencies from source compilation through extraction, interpretation, obligations, automation, solver results, and proof checking.
rationale: A foundational logic does not automatically justify the surrounding pipeline. Anneal must expose every unchecked dependency and a route to replacing trust with evidence.

title: Open-library verification and arbitrary safe clients
question: Determine what evidence supports a safe abstraction used by any permitted client, including generic and separately compiled clients.
rationale: Zerocopy exposes safe APIs over unsafe implementations. Verification must account for all permitted clients, rather than only selected harnesses.

title: Rust's semantic authorities and unresolved rules
question: Compare the Reference, standard-library contracts, compiler behavior, operational-semantics work, and their exact authority and applicability.
rationale: Rust semantics are distributed across sources. Their authority and unresolved areas determine which premises Anneal can justify and which must remain explicit assumptions.

title: Rust core calculi and executable formalizations
question: Compare λRust, Oxide, Featherweight Rust, Rust Distilled, and KRust for reusable definitions and omissions relevant to unsafe code.
rationale: Core calculi can provide useful borrowing and typing results, but their simplifications must be understood before transferring those results to concrete unsafe Rust.

title: MiniRust as an operational foundation
question: Investigate its memory model, executable semantics, Rust-to-MiniRust connection, and prospects for theorem-prover integration.
rationale: An executable Rust-oriented semantics could supply a shared interpretation and discriminating tests; its coverage and proof integration require direct investigation.

title: MIR as Anneal's semantic extraction boundary
question: Examine places, temporaries, promotions, retagging, drops, unwinding, intrinsics, and transformations that can erase relevant behavior.
rationale: Extraction must preserve behavior relevant to UB freedom. Looking only at the final translated model cannot reveal effects removed earlier.

title: LLBC semantics and implemented translation correspondence
question: Separate the formal LLBC results from evidence about the actual rustc–Charon–Aeneas implementation.
rationale: Formal results about modeled languages and correctness of the deployed translator are separate obligations; the research must establish what each contributes.

title: Pointer provenance models
question: Compare allocation identity, strict and exposed provenance, integer-pointer round trips, address reuse, and relevant C provenance work.
rationale: Numerical addresses and bounds alone do not establish access rights. Provenance is essential for pointer operations and interoperability.

title: Stacked Borrows as a verification model
question: Examine its operational rules, proved properties, compatibility constraints, and requirements for a modular program logic.
rationale: It supplies a concrete aliasing model and optimization-related results whose applicability must be compared with the abstractions Anneal needs.

title: Tree Borrows and emerging aliasing logics
question: Evaluate the operational model, mechanized results, and recent work on modular unsafe-Rust aliasing verification.
rationale: A resource logic must justify Rust aliasing obligations, not only heap disjointness; newer aliasing research may change the available design options.

title: Language validity and abstract-machine bytes
question: Study initializedness, invalid values, pointer-bearing bytes, padding, niches, and when validity obligations arise.
rationale: Zerocopy manipulates representations. Treating memory as ordinary integers or typed values can lose precisely the information required for its soundness proofs.

title: Formal data layout and ABI correspondence
question: Cover sized types, DSTs, packing, alignment, enums, SIMD, target dependence, and compiler-layout premises.
rationale: The PR stack proves layout mathematics while retaining compiler premises. This report determines how far existing formalizations can justify that boundary.

title: Rust concurrency semantics
question: Examine atomic ordering, data races, fences, compiler transformations, and the relationship to C/C++ memory models.
rationale: Concurrent separation logic must be paired with an appropriate language memory model; sequential interleaving alone cannot establish all Rust concurrency claims.

title: Compatibility between semantic models
question: Determine how to relate models with different borrowing, provenance, byte, and concurrency rules; include recent source-level trace semantics and async models.
rationale: Combining components requires justified semantic relationships. Similar terminology or overlapping examples does not establish that their guarantees compose.

title: Iris's semantic foundation and adequacy theorem
question: Identify the operational-semantics interface, weakest-precondition construction, and theorem needed to turn logical proofs into execution guarantees.
rationale: This is the foundational connection between resource proofs and program behavior; it determines what a new Rust instance must supply.

title: Resource algebras for Rust memory
question: Evaluate cameras for allocation ownership, byte ranges, initializedness, provenance, permissions, and authoritative state.
rationale: The resource representation controls what can be split, shared, updated, and framed. It must preserve zerocopy's byte-level distinctions.

title: Step-indexing and recursive Rust invariants
question: Examine recursive types, higher-order state, guarded recursion, later modalities, and their practical proof consequences.
rationale: Rich recursive invariants may require this machinery. Its expressive benefits and authoring costs influence whether it belongs in Anneal's core or an extension.

title: Lifetime and borrowing logics
question: Study lifetime tokens, inclusion, shortening, nested borrows, reborrowing, and recovery of ownership when borrows end.
rationale: Lifetime erasure is an explicit Anneal concern. Logical lifetime resources offer a candidate way to preserve the obligations needed at unsafe boundaries.

title: Prophecy mechanisms
question: Compare ordinary and parametric prophecies, their consistency conditions, and their role in mutable-borrow specifications.
rationale: Prophecies connect a borrow's current state to its eventual returned state, making them central to several functional verification approaches.

title: Shared invariants and interior mutability
question: Examine invariant opening, masks, fractional resources, shared ownership, and protocols for UnsafeCell-based abstractions.
rationale: Safe shared APIs often encapsulate mutation. Their proofs need controlled protocols that preserve client reasoning despite aliasing.

title: Logical atomicity and concurrent abstraction boundaries
question: Study logically atomic specifications, interference, synchronization protocols, and ownership transfer between threads.
rationale: These mechanisms may let clients use concurrent abstractions compositionally without reopening their implementation proofs.

title: Termination and liveness beyond safety
question: Compare credits, obligations, fairness assumptions, transfinite techniques, and their interaction with partial correctness.
rationale: Anneal supports promises beyond UB freedom. The design must distinguish safety from termination and progress without foreclosing future liveness properties.

title: Iris in Lean implementation and theorem coverage
question: Audit exact source, proof-mode support, automation, library dependencies, missing constructions, and compatibility with Anneal's Lean pin.
rationale: A Lean implementation could reduce cross-prover integration costs, but its actual theorem and construction coverage must be established before relying on it.

title: RustBelt's reusable semantic typing architecture
question: Reconstruct its abstraction-soundness argument and identify which Rust features require additional semantics or translation evidence.
rationale: RustBelt directly addresses unsafe implementations behind safe abstractions; its proof architecture and modeled-language limits are highly relevant to Anneal.

title: RustHornBelt's bridge from resources to functional contracts
question: Examine semantic typing, parametric prophecies, first-order specifications, and the remaining connection to concrete verification tools.
rationale: This work investigates how resource-sensitive unsafe implementations can justify simpler client contracts, a promising composition boundary.

title: Automation in the Iris ecosystem
question: Compare MoSeL, Lithium, Diaframe, and Quiver for resource reasoning, inference, extension mechanisms, and generated proof evidence.
rationale: Foundational expressiveness must be usable in practice. Existing automation may reduce proof burden while keeping accepted evidence independently checkable.

title: RefinedRust's semantic model and adequacy
question: Audit what its refinement typing establishes about safe and unsafe Rust, under which operational and layout assumptions.
rationale: Its foundational approach to concrete unsafe Rust makes it a direct candidate for reusing semantic definitions and proof structure.

title: RefinedRust's extraction and proof workflow
question: Examine compiler integration, supported MIR, annotations, generated Rocq proofs, manual obligations, and maintenance costs.
rationale: A strong theorem is not sufficient for adoption. This establishes the practical work required to verify Anneal's input programs.

title: Gillian-Rust's symbolic resource model
question: Investigate its implementation of lifetime reasoning and parametric prophecies, supported unsafe operations, and trust boundary.
rationale: Its automation of Rust-specific resources may offer a practical unsafe implementation verifier or inform Anneal's own symbolic engine.

title: The Gillian-Rust–Creusot specification bridge
question: Reconstruct how unsafe implementation evidence supports safe-client contracts; test whether Anneal could use a corresponding boundary.
rationale: A demonstrated hybrid integration provides a concrete architecture to study, including its specification correspondence and remaining trusted connections.

title: VeriFast's Rust verification model
question: Examine ownership predicates, lifetime handling, safe abstractions, concurrency, and correspondence to Rust's aliasing restrictions.
rationale: It supplies another modular separation-logic approach against which to compare expressiveness, automation, and specification effort.

question: Audit emitted Rocq proofs, axiomatic semantics, certificate coverage, and prospects for independent checking or Lean integration.
rationale: Certificate-producing verification may let Anneal reuse automation while controlling the checking boundary and trusted computing base.

rationale: Language changes and rewrites affect adoption and correspondence. Their costs must be visible in comparisons.

rationale: Creusot provides a concrete contract-oriented design for ordinary Rust authors and a useful candidate for automated client verification.

rationale: C verification has substantial reusable infrastructure. A Rust-to-C route is useful only with adequate preservation of Rust-specific obligations.

rationale: A Rust symbolic execution engine may provide useful automation or counterexamples; its coverage and checking boundary determine the role it can safely play.

rationale: Bounds and non-overlap are necessary ingredients, but splitting safe views also requires preservation and distribution of logical access permissions.

title: Type-invariant preservation across all access paths
question: Examine constructors, mutation, public fields, modules, callbacks, destructors, and unannotated code.
rationale: Anneal's open invariant issues show why checking only annotated functions can miss safe operations that violate an invariant.

title: Unsafe-trait laws and implementation evidence
question: Cover dictionaries, associated items, blanket implementations, coinduction, specialization, and downstream implementations.
rationale: A generic proof is sound only when the trait evidence it consumes establishes the relevant laws for every permitted implementation.

title: Transmutation as a relation between admissible states
question: Compare directional validity, mutation compatibility, surviving source views, metadata, and representation correspondence.
rationale: Pointer transmutation can leave several typed views alive. Preserving their obligations requires more than equality of size or a one-way validity implication.

title: By-value transmutation and ownership transfer
question: Model successful conversion, failure recovery, destructor suppression, representation stability, and exactly-once ownership.
rationale: By-value conversion has distinct ownership and drop obligations, including preserving the representation that was actually validated.

title: Partial initialization and destruction
question: Cover MaybeUninit, ManuallyDrop, partial aggregates, unwinding, leaks, forget, and double-drop prevention.
rationale: These operations are common unsafe implementation tools, and their cleanup and ownership behavior can disappear in a value-only model.

title: Allocation and container growth
question: Cover allocation identity, allocator contracts, reallocation, zeroing, OOM, Vec capacity, and address stability.
rationale: Layout arithmetic alone cannot establish that storage exists, remains alive, or is correctly transferred during growth.

title: DST and packed-layout access

rationale: These behaviors stress lifetime and ownership models across suspension and destruction, testing the architecture's extension path.

rationale: Unsafe Rust interacts with behavior outside a Rust heap model. Anneal needs compositional, visible assumptions at these boundaries.
